# a x + y of two limbs, a of T, a, x and y stored

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `axpy_step_2_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $a x + y$:

$$z \approx a x + y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`axpy_entry_step_2_1`](axpy_entry_step_2_1.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - (a x + y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 2u u)}{1 - 4u} + 2\right) u^2\,(\lvert a x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert) + \tfrac{5}{4}\,\eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $\approx 6.163 \times 10^{-32}$ | $\approx 1.7764 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $5 \cdot 2^{-1076} \approx 6.1758 \times 10^{-324}$ | $5 \cdot 2^{-151} \approx 1.7516 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.4000000000002p-104`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.400004p-46f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `axpy_step_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/MapSteps.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/MapSteps.v), against `axpy_step_2_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions axpy_step_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition axpy_step_2_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (3 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let '(z0, z1) := axpy_step_2_1 emin prec tie_even a x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((a * (x0 + x1)) + (y0 + y1))) <= (((3 * (1 + ((2 * u prec) * u prec))) / (1 - (4 * u prec))) + 2) * u prec ^ 2 * (Rabs (a * (x0 + x1)) + Rabs (y0 + y1)) + (5 / 4) * eta emin.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `axpy_step_2_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the step of axpy (milestone2.md, "sum, dot, axpy, convolution"): the product, then the sum, mul_2_1 ([JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 9) then add_2_2 ([JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 6); bounds from [MR22](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#mr22). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/axpy_step_2_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/axpy_step_2_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md), [`add_2_2`](add_2_2.md).

```
# The step of axpy_2_1: z = (x a) + y with a scalar a of T, mul_2_1 then add_2_2 (milestone2.md:
# mul_2_1 when the scalar of axpy is a T). The step of axpy_2_1, on a stored scalar and stored
# arrays, written through Kairn: kairn::axpy calls axpy_2_1_entry, whose step axpy_entry_step_2_1
# guards a and every limb of x and y and then runs this one (rule R3, the factors of a fused
# operation). Not an entry kernel.
# Its bound, relative to the terms |a x| + |y|, from those of mul_2_1 (2u^2, eta) and add_2_2, with
# eps+ = 3u^2/(1-4u): |z - (a x + y)| <= (eps+ (1 + 2u^2) + 2u^2) |a x| + eps+ |y| + (1 + eps+) eta,
# and 1 + eps+ <= 5/4 from precision 3.

(p0, p1) = mul_2_1(x0, x1, a)
(z0, z1) = add_2_2(p0, p1, y0, y1)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#axpy_step_2_1)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 666 768 | 0 | 0.800000 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 669 342 | 0 | 0.800000 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats | 1 373 185 | 0 | 0.641498 (`fp:4:-5:-3`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
